_source.citation: McGhee, R. J., Walker, B. S., and Millard, B. F., 'Experimental Results for the Eppler 387 Airfoil at Low Reynolds Numbers in the Langley Low-Turbulence Pressure Tunnel', NASA TM-4062, October 1988.
_source.digitized_by: hand-read from the scanned Appendix B computer listing (Table B1) and Table III, rendered at 3.2x with PyMuPDF and read visually; 2026-07-29
_source.corrected_data_note: Table B1 lists the wall/blockage-corrected section coefficients (c_m about the quarter chord); these are the values plotted.

_selection_criterion: For the alpha=5 Reynolds-sweep figure, every increasing-alpha row in Table B1 with |alpha - 5.00 deg| <= 0.10 is included as an individual measurement (its own black circle). Hysteresis (decreasing-alpha) runs are excluded because none of their rows fall within 0.10 deg of alpha=5 (nearest are ~4.0 and ~6.0 deg). The 60k bistable lift collapse (alpha=5.51 -> c_l=0.639) and the alpha=4.00 repeat triple are recorded below under _excluded but NOT plotted at alpha=5 (they belong to the bistability discussion).

300000.table: B1 (Experimental Results From Langley Low-Turbulence Pressure Tunnel)

table_III_oilflow_alpha5._note: Table III (report p.11, pdf page index 14), 'Upper Surface Chordwise Locations (x/c) of Separation and Reattachment From Oil Flow Visualization'. LS = laminar separation, TR = turbulent reattachment. Tabulated at alpha=5 for R=100k/200k/300k ONLY; there is no 60k or 460k oil-flow closure at alpha=5 in this source (60k oil flow is not tabulated; the 460k column is absent from Table III). This confirms the prior rework: no extension possible.

_excluded_not_plotted._note: Recorded for provenance / bistability discussion; NOT part of the alpha=5 comparison.
